subject: Biotechnology
title: Antibody Mimetics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Antibody Mimetics.

hook.text: Antibodies are great but bulky, expensive, and need cold storage — can we build something better?

buildup.text: DARPins are engineered repeat proteins — small, stable, and produced cheaply in bacteria.

discovery.text: Affibodies are 58 amino acids — they bind targets as tightly as antibodies but are 20 times smaller.

twist.text: Aptamers are not proteins at all — they are folded nucleic acids that bind targets like molecular origami.

climax.text: Abicipar, a DARPin for wet macular degeneration, lasted longer than ranibizumab — fewer injections needed.

punchline.text: Beyond antibodies — mimetics offer new shapes for old problems.

quiz.question: What advantage do antibody mimetics offer over traditional antibodies?
options: They always work better than antibodies in clinical trials
They are smaller, more stable, and cheaper to produce while binding targets with similar affinity
They do not require any regulatory approval before use
